title: Standard input and output: data contracts and a verifiable project
goal: Read two numbers and identify input, computation and output.

prerequisites.text: You know if/else, ||, !, int and multiplication; stream state is introduced here.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: stdin is the program’s input text. Enter 4 3 in the input field: std::cin >> width >> height attempts to read two integers. A space or newline separates them. After successful input, width=4 and height=3. std::cout is a separate output; it does not populate stdin.

!(std::cin >> width >> height) is true when reading fails: ! negates the stream’s successful state. An early return ends main, so a failed read never reaches area calculation. width<0 || height<0 rejects negative sizes. Use dimensions 0..1000 for this example; upper bounds are checked before multiplication too.

This small protocol reads two numbers and does not require the absence of later words. Strict whole-line parsing and mixing cin with getline are separate later steps. Empty stdin produces invalid here, unlike examples containing data directly in the source.

sections.title: Read two numbers and identify input, computation and output.
trace: Both integers were read, so the first branch is skipped.
Output is computed only after the two checks.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Keep the source: put 5 6 into stdin, then oops.
The two numeric tokens become width and height.
With oops, reading an int fails and multiplication never runs.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Computing after a failed read uses values not obtained from the user. Check reading before computation.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Read a price and quantity in 0..1000 with read and bounds checks. Print the product or invalid. Check 70 5, 70 0, -1 5 and empty input.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Keep the source: put 5 6 into stdin, then oops.
selfcheck.feedback: The two numeric tokens become width and height. With oops, reading an int fails and multiplication never runs.

selfcheck.prompt: Read a price and quantity in 0..1000 with read and bounds checks. Print the product or invalid. Check 70 5, 70 0, -1 5 and empty input.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. For inputs 70 5, 70 0, -1 5 and empty input, the answers are 350, 0, invalid, invalid. Calculation must not run after a failed read or a bounds violation.

modulePracticum.title: Module project: verifiable file-transfer time
modulePracticum.label: MODULE 2 PROJECT
modulePracticum.challenge: Implement a MiB-to-kbit/s transfer model with overhead, upward rounding, and strict finite input.
modulePracticum.readiness: All 12 lessons. Use main, long long, conditions, and streams; no loops, new/delete, or authored functions are required.

skills.title: Your first C++ program: from source to a verifiable report
Tokens and names: precise source with clear meaning
Comments, constants, and literals: meaning instead of magic numbers
Data types: choosing values, initialization, and measuring a target
Variables, blocks, and lifetime: a state journal
Expressions and operators: grouping, values, and clear steps
Arithmetic and assignment: quotient, remainder, and safe intermediates
Type conversions: intent, information loss, and range checks
Comparisons and logic: conditions as testable contracts
++ and --, sizeof and ?: — concise syntax with precise meaning
Objects, copies, references, and pointers: links without unsafe memory
Standard input and output: data contracts and a verifiable project

requirements: Input m r h with the theory’s ranges: exactly three integer fields.
MiB=1048576 bytes and kbit/s=1000 bit/s; h is a payload-bit percentage.
All intermediate products use long long before the first multiplication.
stdout: seconds minutes remainder and newline; errors: invalid and newline.
Do not add pointers or references to the formula without a purpose; practicum C separately demonstrates that skill.
milestones: Restate units and independently derive four baseline cases.
Complete the starter calculation and stdout.
Prove the numerator upper bound and nonzero denominator.
Run 30 reference cases and two original cases.
walkthrough: 1 MiB contains 8388608 bits. At 1000 kbit/s without overhead it takes 8.388608 seconds, rounded upward to 9.
At h=25 the payload is multiplied by 125/100, producing 10.48576 seconds and rounding to 11.
num/den supplies whole seconds and a nonzero remainder adds one, avoiding a potentially risky num+den−1 sum.
At maximum volume, minimum rate, and 100% overhead, the result is 16777216000 seconds: 279620266 minutes and 40 seconds.
artifacts: main.cpp and a written unit contract.
A table of 30+2 inputs, expectations, and actual stdout.
One defect with hypothesis, repair, and repeat check.
Model limits: constant rate, specified overhead, and no real-network measurement.

terms.definition: Standard input. Nexus supplies a finite character sequence followed by end of input.
Reading a typed value with >> according to parsing and stream-state rules.
Reports failed extraction or a more serious error; a value after failure is not treated as validated input.
Reports end of input already encountered rather than predicting future extraction success.
A library type for a sequence of characters; string algorithms are studied separately.
Reads through a delimiter, usually newline; the delimiter is extracted but not included in the result.
Consumes leading whitespace, including newlines and blank lines, up to a nonwhitespace character or end of input.

blockPracticum.title: Practicum C: objects, aliases, and an input contract
blockPracticum.label: CUMULATIVE PRACTICUM C
blockPracticum.challenge: Read stock, issue at most three, and report snapshot, updated value, and object identity.
blockPracticum.readiness: Lessons 9–12 and state tracing. Addresses are compared rather than printed as fixed numbers.

skills.title: Comparisons and logic: conditions as testable contracts
++ and --, sizeof and ?: — concise syntax with precise meaning
Objects, copies, references, and pointers: links without unsafe memory
Standard input and output: data contracts and a verifiable project

requirements: Exactly one integer within 0…100 and an optional whitespace tail.
The snapshot is independent; alias and selected access live stock.
same_object=1 is checked by pointer equality.
milestones: Update through the reference and read through the pointer.
walkthrough: snapshot copies the initial value. &alias yields stock’s address and selected holds that address.
issued≤stock makes subtraction safe. stock’s lifetime covers all accesses.
artifacts: Eight actual and expected stdout records.
A diagnosed defect without unsafe reads.
